_comment: har-policy.default.json -- the stringent scrub baseline (issue #297, Stage 1).
This file is synced from IntelliSDLC.ai and is NOT the place a consuming
project records its own posture: write .har-policy.project.json instead,
which merges over this file and survives the next sync.
RULES ONLY, NEVER VALUES. Names, patterns and decisions live here and are
reviewable in a diff. A raw identity value belongs in the gitignored
.har-profile.json and nowhere else.
The two axes: a `secret` grants access, an `identity` names a person. Every
secret class gates and a consumer may not lower it -- the sanctioned escape
is a per-value `waiver`, which carries a reason and expires. Identity
classes default to `advise` for shape evidence, because shape carries no
provenance: a Luhn-valid digit run is a card, a trip id, or nothing at all.
Identity LITERALS (declared in .har-profile.json) always gate, whatever the
class setting says.
`identifierFields` names fields whose CONTENTS are an object id. An
IDENTITY-class shape finding whose enclosing field name matches is reported
and does not block: a card-shaped digit run at `media_id` is a card only in
the sense that ~10% of digit runs are. It NEVER applies to a secret class --
a high-entropy token under `session_id` is still a session token. The
entries here are generic patterns only; a specific provider's field name is
a consumer concept and belongs in .har-policy.project.json, which appends.
`cardIssuers` is EMPTY here on purpose. Issuer identification numbers are a
public payment-network standard, so the shipped table lives in har-shapes.js;
this list only ADDS to it, for a market whose cards the standard table does
not name. Additions append and never subtract -- to loosen card detection,
lower classes.identity.credit-card, which is visible as a setting.
